First, we evaluate the inner integral by integrating with respect to $r$, treating $\theta $ as a constant: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi /2}^{2\pi }\,{\int }_{0}^{2}-3{r}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,dr\,d\theta  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{2\pi }[{\int }_{0}^{2}-3{r}^{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,dr]d\theta  \\  & =-3{\int }_{\pi /2}^{2\pi }{[-\frac{{r}^{4}}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )]}_{r=0}^{r=2}\,d\theta  \\  & =-3{\int }_{\pi /2}^{2\pi }(-\frac{{2}^{4}}{4}\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )+0)\,d\theta  \\  & =-3{\int }_{\pi /2}^{2\pi }-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,d\theta \end{aligned}
$$

 

Then, we integrate with respect to $\theta :$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}-3{\int }_{\pi /2}^{2\pi }-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\theta )\,d\theta  & =12[\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\theta )}{2}]_{\pi /2}^{2\pi } \\  & =6(1+1) \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$
